headline: Contrastive and graph encoders for biomolecular interaction and expression prediction
label: Biomolecular Representation Learning
summary: Recent bioinformatics papers pair pretrained, contrastive, and graph encoders with external biological structure to predict molecular interactions and outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of pretrained or external biological structure to shape learned representations for prediction tasks. AbAgKer draws on pre-trained representations and epitope pseudo-structure priors, DynaTCR uses dynamic hard-negative graph ensembles for TCR-epitope binding, and DFCE-KanT applies contrastive learning to predict spatial gene expression from histology images. LFFA reuses frozen foundation-model features for few-shot pathology biomarker prediction, while MRGBMDAT and HMA-GCA apply graph encoding, bilinear fusion, and gated cross-attention to miRNA-disease and circRNA-miRNA associations. Not all items share this emphasis: TRACE reports near-chance results under an audited protocol, and a knowledge graph benchmark shows that train-test redundancy and degree bias inflate link prediction performance. The notable addition across this set is closer attention to evaluation rigor alongside architectural design.
